card.title: 6th INFANTRY BRIGADE
card.text: Deployment: Has 0 operation cost this turn.
card.flavorText: The 6th Lwów Infantry Brigade was one of the main infantry brigades of the Polish 5th Kresowa Infantry Division. It served alongside the 5th Wilno Infantry Brigade, with the 4th Wołyń Infantry Brigade added in 1945. The brigade’s name recalled the city of Lwów and the lost eastern borderlands of the Second Polish Republic, a strong theme in the division’s identity. The 5th Kresowa Infantry Division was formed in the Middle East in March 1943 from Polish forces that had left the Soviet Union and regrouped under Allied command. It became part of General Władysław Anders’ Polish II Corps, serving with the British Eighth Army in the Italian Campaign. The division landed in southern Italy in February 1944 and entered combat the next month. In May, it fought in the final Battle of Monte Cassino, where it suffered a 15% casualty rate. It then took part in the Battle of Ancona, fought near the Gothic Line, and joined the final Allied offensive in 1945, advancing to Bologna. During its service in Italy, the division suffered 5,127 casualties, including 1,063 killed.
